hypothesis: Doubling source-pixel inference resolution may retain finer paper boundaries and improve supported outlines without changing the weights. Scale sensitivity may instead worsen predictions.
protocol: Use each photograph only with its original source/motif-held-out frozen checkpoint; no training or threshold selection.
Preserve the exact continuous full-photo letterbox window. Decode the same source RGB; replay 256px input pixels exactly and verify prediction agreement within 1e-5.
Score both arms on the identical existing 256px partial labels: sample 512px probabilities at those continuous label centres. One global A/B exchange; missing body remains an error.
Inspect all 19 field comparisons. Body/material scores alone do not establish boundary or template quality.
Run crop comparison on all 19 photos with both complete fields, unchanged geometry/support gates and no per-photo best-arm selection. Fit only if this stage gives evidence of improved crops.
No deployment from this diagnostic, no new photos/checkpoints, no bulk duplicate artifacts.
limitations: Previously inspected development photos with two broad source/motif folds; no unseen-generalization claim.
Partial labels omit many uncertain edges and junctions. More pixels do not provide cutting-path ground truth.
Inference at 512px changes feature scale as well as sampling; it is not equivalent to higher-resolution training.
One low-priority CPU thread; inference timings exclude startup, decoding and crop/fitting.
